title: Semantic judgement: the JEV mesh judges UX, with an anti-hallucination guardrail
description: Some correctness questions have no numeric oracle - 'is this warning clear enough?' When the data source truly goes offline, does the cockpit make that unmistakable to the operator?
approach: Argus takes the simulator offline (ground truth), then asks the JEV mesh to judge whether the cockpit clearly warns the operator - requiring it to quote exact on-screen text. Argus verifies the quote against the live DOM and discards any verdict whose evidence is not really there, so an LLM opinion can never raise a false alarm.
steps: [  0.6s] Start: Drone 1 flying, cockpit showing live data
[ 12.0s] Ground truth changes: the flight-data simulator (the source) goes offline
[ 19.1s] No numeric oracle can score 'is the warning clear enough' — so the JEV mesh judges it
